answer: Reputation is computed from normalized, reciprocity-weighted endorsements and their transitive paths, then discounted by an exponential temporal half-life, so an identity must provide sustained honest service to retain influence. An established anchor can earn centrality through consistent reciprocal behavior; newly spawned walnut or shale identities start with near-zero eigenvector centrality, and cannot manufacture trust through a burst of self-created accounts or pass consensus without credible support.
